newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: Sao Tome rocked by protests over fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Sao Tome rocked by protests over fuel prices.

text.p: Hundreds of protesters, many armed with knives, marched on the presidential palace in central Sao Tome on Wednesday, slashing car tyres and shouting slogans against a recently decreed doubling in fuel prices.

Witnesses said heavily armed police were guarding the presidential residence and government buildings in the capital of the impoverished Atlantic archipelago of Sao Tome and Principe, scene of an aborted military coup 20 months ago.

Popular anger erupted on Monday after the government of President Miguel Trovoada announced that petrol prices would be doubled to some $0.65 per litre (0.26 gallon) in line with a financial plan agreed with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
The former Portuguese colony, 125 miles (200 km) off the coast of Gabon, has a foreign debt of $340 million which it is unable to finance and desperately needs aid to fund development projects.
Witnesses said the disturbances were led by taxi and lorry drivers who were blocking main streets in the capital of the small twin-island state with a population of some 120,000.
Many shops and schools were closed on Wednesday for fear of trouble.

On Tuesday, a TAP-Air Portugal plane bringing Prime Minister Paul Braganca and a team of IMF and World Bank officials from Lisbon had been forced to circle the islands' airport while burning tyres were cleared from the runway.
Trovoada was briefly held prisoner in August 1995 by disgruntled army officials who staged an uprising in protest at poor pay and conditions.
